cases.description: Verify that calling Base64.builder() returns a non-null Builder object.

cases.expected: two distinct Builder instances on successive calls
cases.description: Ensure that each invocation of Base64.builder() creates a new Builder instance (different object references).
Confirm that the returned object's runtime type is exactly Base64.Builder.

cases.expected: Base64 instance where isUrlSafe() returns false and getLineSeparator() returns null (default configuration)
cases.description: Validate that a Builder created with Base64.builder() and built without any further configuration produces a Base64 object using the library's default settings (non‑URL‑safe and no custom line separator).

cases.expected: Base64 instance where isUrlSafe() returns true
cases.description: Verify that invoking the urlSafe() option on the Builder (Base64.builder().urlSafe().build()) yields a Base64 object that reports URL‑safe mode via isUrlSafe().

cases.expected: Base64 instance whose getLineSeparator() returns a byte array equal to {13,10}
cases.description: Check that supplying a custom line separator via withLineSeparator(new byte[]{'\r','\n'}) on the Builder results in a Base64 object that returns the same separator from getLineSeparator().
Calling withLineSeparator(null) on a Builder should throw NullPointerException because a null line separator is not allowed.
Calling withLineSeparator(new byte[]{}) (empty array) on a Builder should throw IllegalArgumentException because the line separator cannot be empty.
Calling withLineSeparator(new byte[]{'A','B','C'}) (array length not a multiple of 2) on a Builder should throw IllegalArgumentException because the line separator must consist of CR/LF pair(s).
Invoking build() on a Builder after calling withLineSeparator(new byte[]{'\r','\n','\r','\n','\r'}) (invalid length) should result in IllegalStateException during validation in the build process.
